source_text: Desine itaque viros sani capitis et Ecclesiarum antistites criminari; non subiciantur iudicio negligentiora commenta; neque enim iram cunctatio brevis, sed pertinax meretur intentio. Imitemur sane eorum illud studium, quo populos aedificaverunt exhortando, obsecrando, coarguendo; quorum num quidquam fecissent, si vestro more peccata non voluntaria, sed naturalia credidissent?
pass_a_gloss: Cease therefore to accuse men of a sound head and overseers of the Churches; let the more negligent inventions not be subjected to judgment; for not a brief delay, but a pertinacious intention, deserves wrath. Let us indeed imitate that zeal of theirs by which they built up peoples by exhorting, beseeching, convicting; of which would they have done anything, if in your manner they had believed sins not voluntary but natural?

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Stop accusing men of sound mind and leaders of churches. Let less careful remarks not be brought to judgment: a brief hesitation does not deserve anger, but a stubborn intention does. Let us instead imitate the zeal with which they built up their peoples by exhorting, beseeching, and rebuking. Would they have done any of this if, like you, they had believed sins natural rather than voluntary?

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
